gap: No result ChatGPT got states the Docker Engine version each NAS OS ships, or how that compares with the Docker API v1.44 that Nextcloud AIO uses by default. UGREEN UGOS Pro (29.6.2, API ≤1.55), ASUSTOR (29.6.2), QNAP Container Station (27.1.2, API 1.46) and TerraMaster TOS (27.2.1, API 1.47) all meet it. Synology DSM Container Manager (24.0.2, API 1.43), on the DS925+ and DS225+, is the only one below it. AIO's Docker socket proxy and AppAPI fail there unless you override the API version, which the AIO maintainers say they don't support or test.
standout_why: I checked the rival pages ChatGPT got. racksandwatts.com (cited), esp32.co.uk best-4-bay (cited) and nasdrives.ca best-for-nextcloud name only the container app ('UGOS Pro Docker', 'Container Manager', 'Runs well in Docker'). None gives an engine or API version or mentions any AIO incompatibility. The cited AIO readme says Synology users 'likely need to adjust the internally used api version', but it gives no numbers and doesn't compare brands. Issue #7365 (a result, not cited) has DSM's API 1.43 against the 1.44 AIO needs, but only for Synology. No page puts all the brands in one comparable column, and our current page doesn't either.
decides: This backs the UGREEN DXP4800 Plus or DXP2800 as the pick for running Nextcloud AIO as shipped, and it weakens the DS925+, which ChatGPT called the 'best software experience' or 'best overall'. On DSM, AIO needs the DOCKER_API_VERSION override that the maintainers don't support, or the Docker Socket Proxy (needed by AppAPI/ExApps) turned off. Synology has kept Container Manager on Docker 24.0.2, which reached end of life in June 2024, through its August 2026 package update. QNAP and TerraMaster meet 1.44 but run older engines than UGREEN and ASUSTOR. Footnote for the table: the 'Docker support' tick every rival shows is not equal across brands.
